claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or NVQs up to level 3) or approved training (such as an unpaid traineeship)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in sixth form studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Studying A-levels at sixth form counts as approved education, which is good for eligibility.

Now, could you tell me about your living situation:

Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Is anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question to confirm eligibility:

Does Alex work 24 hours or more per week, or does he receive any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's focused on his studies. And he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ You live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ Alex lives with you, meaning you're responsible for him
- ✅ Although Alex is 16, he's in approved education (A-levels at sixth form)
- ✅ Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week
- ✅ Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own right
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex while he remains in approved education, up until he turns 20.

If you haven't already, you can make a claim for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old and is in approved education (studying A-levels at sixth form). His parent lives in the UK and Alex lives with them, meaning the parent is responsible for him. No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Alex does not work 24 hours or more per week and does not receive any benefits in his own right. All eligibility criteria are met for Child Benefit to continue for a child aged 16-19 who remains in approved education.
